questions.q: What are the three types of attention described in the summary?
a: Focused, sorting and open
Active, passive and divided
Visual, auditory and kinesthetic
Narrow, broad and sustained
questions.why: Lesson 1 divides attention into focused attention, sorting and open attention, each useful in different situations.

questions.q: What is open attention especially useful for?
a: Accessing memories and images to create new ideas
Concentrating on one task while ignoring distractions
Comparing options before forming a final opinion
Following a step-by-step procedure without error
questions.why: The summary says open attention lets focus diffuse, giving us access to memories and images that spark new thoughts.

questions.q: What does Markova suggest for communicating better with others?
a: Learn your own mind patterns and ask what helps others
Stick to one communication style in every setting
Copy the habits of the most productive colleague
Avoid small meetings and rely on written reports
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends understanding your own working style, then asking people which communication tools help them most.

questions.q: What routine does the author suggest to engage a team's creativity?
a: Standing up or walking around during sessions
Working in total silence with no breaks
Holding only large brainstorming meetings
Assigning everyone the same thinking style
questions.why: The summary describes a moving-around routine where team members stand or walk to work more dynamically.

questions.q: What does the right hemisphere of the brain favor, according to the summary?
a: Feelings, teamwork, morale and human connection
Facts, data, numbers and rational analysis
Operations, tactics and step-by-step processes
Rules, hierarchy and formal reporting
questions.why: Lesson 3 places relational thinking and innovation in the right hemisphere, while facts and procedure sit on the left.
